solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rebuild statue or it will be face down

indicators.note: to rebuild is to put the parts together again in a new form, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sculptor is told to remake a statue, or else it will end up toppled on its face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face down' looks like part of the statue's fate, but it is the definition: to face someone down is to stare them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To face down an opponent is to confront them until they back off, which is what staring them out achieves.

clue.text: Technically connected with how fish may be caught

definitions.meaning: ... means connected to a computer network
fish are caught on a line when angling

explanation.surface: An angler's computer link is described along with the method of fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being linked to the internet is called being online, and a hooked fish is literally on a line.

clue.text: Announcer's personal credit level is restricting

definitions.note: read as Announcer is, the 's being the link to the wordplay

indicators.note: restricting says the level holds the other pieces confined inside it

parts.note: a tier is a level
your own is personal to you
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's own credit rating is holding them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announcer's' is read as 'Announcer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was the official who called out public announcements in the streets.

clue.text: Weight lifting men not in the majority

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the letters are read upward, in reverse
in the majority says the answer lies within the letters of men not, taking most of them

explanation.surface: Weightlifting is described as something most men do not do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the majority' takes ENNOT, most of the letters of 'men not', and 'lifting' turns it up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonne is a metric unit of weight, one thousand kilograms.

clue.text: Old setter desperate for award

indicators.note: desperate suggests wildness, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An ageing crossword setter is longing for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize, for example at a show.

clue.text: Breathlessness due to open conflict in support group

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters sit inside the support group's letters

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, the best-known support group

indicators.note: conflict suggests things at odds and thrown about, so the letters of open are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone at a support meeting gasps for breath because open hostility has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is the crossword's stock support group; 'conflict' looks like the fight but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Apnoea is the medical term for a temporary stopping of breathing, as in sleep apnoea.

clue.text: Board dogged by quiz

parts.note: a board of people is a panel
game means plucky and determined, as dogged is

explanation.surface: A committee is pursued relentlessly by questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel game is a broadcast quiz in which a team of guests answer questions.

clue.text: Test constituents as extras

definitions.meaning: a Test match in cricket is made up of ..., sets of six balls

explanation.surface: Parts of an exam are counted as additional items.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; an over is a set of six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Overs are the units a cricket innings is divided into, and in another sense amounts in excess.

clue.text: Nothing attained without a complex cure

indicators.note: complex means intricately mixed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: without says the letter a is removed from attained

explanation.surface: A complicated remedy is achieved from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops A from ATTAINED; 'complex' shuffles O with TTAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts a poison, a kind of cure.

clue.text: Some backward tribes send welcoming obscenity

indicators.note: backward says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An anthropologist's report that some primitive tribes greet visitors with rude gestures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks SSENDWEL out of 'tribes send welcoming', and 'backward' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewdness is crude, indecent behaviour or talk, which is what an obscenity is.

clue.text: Absorb sound of joking

indicators.note: sound of says the answer is a word that is heard like the phrase for joking

parts.note: joking means in jest

explanation.surface: An instruction to take in the noise of people having a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, a physical kind of absorbing.

clue.text: Still Gaff is a beast

parts.note: still in the sense of even now means yet
the setter Gaff refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter claims to remain a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the legendary ape-like creature of the Himalayas, so a beast.

clue.text: Specialist in Masonic heraldry

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the letters of the two words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone is an expert in the coats of arms of the Freemasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specialist' looks like a person, but it is an adjective here: a niche market is a specialist one.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, niche describes a product or interest aimed at a small specialised group.

clue.text: Crisscrossed wasteland clutching bad back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled string is then read in reverse
clutching says the wasteland holds the other word inside it

parts.note: a desert is a barren wasteland
bad as in unwell means ill

explanation.surface: Tracks cross a desert that is gripping someone with a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of 'bad back', a sore spine, but it reverses DESILLERT, made when 'clutching' puts ILL into DESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellised surface is covered with a lattice of crossing strips, so it is crisscrossed.

clue.text: Diminutive race found in outskirts of Lille

indicators.note: found in says the race sits inside what is left of the city name
outskirts of keeps only the edges of the city name, dropping its centre letter

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A small race is held on the edge of the French city of Lille.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' drops the central letter, keeping both edges of the city name. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminutive means very small, a plain synonym of little.

clue.text: Arrangement for sister to embrace No 10's banality

indicators.note: to embrace says the shuffled letters hold the number inside them
an arrangement for something puts it into a new order, so the letters of sister are rearranged

parts.note: number ten is TEN, the 's reading as is to link to the definition

explanation.surface: A sister is lined up to hug a Downing Street figure, which is all rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement for' shuffles the sister into TRIESS. No 10 is Downing Street, home of the UK Prime Minister, but here it is simply the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Triteness is the quality of being overused and unoriginal, which is banality.

clue.text: See 21 down
Blue about charge initially taken for bubbly

indicators.note: about here means turned around and shuffled, so the letters of Blue are rearranged

parts.note: a lien is a legal charge on property

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of taken

explanation.surface: A melancholy figure, accused of something, is first taken for champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes EBUL from BLUE. 'bubbly' looks like champagne but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means cheerful and full of energy, which is what a bubbly person is.

clue.text: Ran from skinhead robbed outside library entrance

parts.note: the head of skin is its first letter, S

indicators.note: outside says the robbed word goes around the library's first letter

parts.note: to be mugged is to be robbed in the street

indicators.note: entrance is the start of library, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone fled from a thug who had been robbed at the library door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' looks like fled, but it is the sense of running goods past customs. 'skinhead' gives S, the head of 'skin'.
explanation.definitionFit: To run contraband is to smuggle it, so ran can mean smuggled.

clue.text: When newspapers appear to report grief

indicators.note: to report suggests speaking, so the answer is heard like the word for grief

parts.note: mourning is the expression of grief

explanation.surface: The papers come out with grim news of loss to share.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily newspapers are delivered and sold early in the day, so morning is their time.

clue.text: Oddly, Goldeneye starts with happiness

indicators.note: starts says only the opening run of those odd letters is used, the last being dropped
Oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of Goldeneye

explanation.surface: A Bond film opens on a cheerful note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' gives GLEEE from GOLDENEYE; 'starts' keeps the first four.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight, a near synonym of happiness.

clue.text: Cross fire damaged centre of Hull

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of fire are knocked out of order
centre of takes the middle letters of Hull

explanation.surface: A fire has wrecked the middle of the city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns FIRE into IREF; 'centre of' gives UL from HULL. Hull is a port city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireful means full of ire, that is angry, which is a sense of cross.

clue.text: Apology from Gaff that it's impossible to solve 6d

definitions.text: Apology from Gaff that it's impossible to solve
definitions.meaning: the setter saying sorry and admitting he cannot crack it says ...
6d is PANEL GAME; this is the title of a radio panel game

annotation.spelling: I'M SORRY I HAVEN'T A CLUE

explanation.surface: The setter apologises, confessing the puzzle cannot be cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 6d is PANEL GAME. The answer is a long-running BBC Radio 4 comedy panel show.
explanation.definitionFit: I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue is a famous British radio comedy quiz, an example of a panel game.

clue.text: Good opening for toffs

parts.note: an entry is an opening or way in

explanation.surface: A fine chance for the upper classes to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: Toffs is British slang for posh upper-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the landed upper class, the people mocked as toffs.

clue.text: I leave rebellious grenadiers to shoot growers

indicators.note: rebellious soldiers break ranks, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leave says the letter I departs from the soldiers' word

explanation.surface: A soldier quits mutinous guardsmen who are about to fire on farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' removes I from GRENADIERS, and 'rebellious' shuffles GRENADERS. 'shoot' looks like firing, but shoots are new plant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners raise plants, which put out shoots, so they are growers of shoots.

clue.text: Full of plants reserved under code

indicators.note: under in a down clue places the first word's letters beneath the code

parts.note: RU is rugby union, one of the football codes
a reserved person is shy

explanation.surface: A garden thick with greenery is kept back under a secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union and the other football games are called codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushy describes ground full of rushes, the marsh plants.

clue.text: See 21 down
Pose with a struggling author

indicators.note: struggling suggests twisting about, so the letters of Pose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer strikes an attitude while having a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek writer credited with the famous animal fables.

clue.text: Tune in to cant with vacant expression

parts.note: to cant is to tilt or lean, which is to list

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so only the first and last letters of expression remain

explanation.surface: Someone tunes in to hypocritical talk while wearing a blank look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cant' looks like humbug talk, but it means to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune in to something is to pay attention to it, an idiomatic way of saying listen.

clue.text: Bowed to the moon sometimes

definitions.meaning: bowed means curved like a bow
the moon appears as a ... at some phases

explanation.surface: Someone bows to the moon now and then, as in a ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent is a curved shape like a bow, and it is the form of the moon in its early and late phases.

clue.text: Most exhausted doctor agreed to opening

parts.note: saying yes means you agreed

indicators.note: opening refers to the start of the word to, its first letter

explanation.surface: A worn-out doctor says yes to an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exhausted has been used up or drained, so the most exhausted well or source is the driest.

clue.text: Understanding Gaff's return route in classy ending

indicators.note: in says these pieces sit within the end of classy
ending keeps only the final stretch of the word classy
return says the setter's possessive word is turned round

parts.note: the setter Gaff's things are my things
a path is a route

explanation.surface: The setter finds an understanding way home in a stylish finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses MY to YM; with PATH it goes 'in' SY, the 'ending' of CLASSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathy is fellow feeling, sharing or understanding another person's situation.
